citations.quote: A **filtered chain complex** $(C,d,F)$ in an abelian category is a chain complex with increasing filtrations $F_pC_n\subseteq C_n$ for all $n$, whose pieces form subcomplexes. The conventions are [[def-increasing-and-decreasing-filtration-of-an-object]] and [[def-subcomplex]]. Thus, in modules, the condition is exactly $d_n(F_pC_n)\subseteq F_pC_{n-1}$; a factorization implies the inclusion, and the inclusion defines the restricted function. No finite-bound hypothesis is implicit.

Its Maslov index is the Fredholm index of the linearized disk equation. The candidate differential sends $x$ to the mod-two sum of $y$ over index-one holomorphic Whitney disks with multiplicity zero at $z$. The homology of this chain complex, when the analytic and move-invariance results hold, is denoted $\widehat{HF}(Y;\mathbb F_2)$.

citations.quote: A **filtered chain complex** $(C,d,F)$ in an abelian category is a chain complex with increasing filtrations $F_pC_n\subseteq C_n$ for all $n$, whose pieces form subcomplexes. Explicitly $d_n$ factors as $F_pC_n\to F_pC_{n-1}$ on each piece. These restrictions square to zero since their composites with the monic inclusion into $C_{n-2}$ are $d_{n-1}d_n=0$. The conventions are [[def-increasing-and-decreasing-filtration-of-an-object]] and [[def-subcomplex]]. Thus, in modules, the condition is exactly $d_n(F_pC_n)\subseteq F_pC_{n-1}$; a factorization implies the inclusion, and the inclusion defines the restricted function. No finite-bound hypothesis is implicit.

A **homological spectral sequence** in an abelian category ([[def-abelian-category]]), starting at a specified integer $r_0\ge0$, consists of objects $E^r_{p,q}$, maps
$$d^r_{p,q}:E^r_{p,q}\to E^r_{p-r,q+r-1},\qquad d^rd^r=0,$$
for r≥r₀ and p,q∈ℤ, and specified isomorphisms
$$\alpha_r:\frac{\ker(d^r_{p,q})}{\operatorname{im}(d^r_{p+r,q-r+1})}\xrightarrow{\sim}E^{r+1}_{p,q}.$$
The quotient has the meaning of [[def-homology-object-of-a-chain-complex]]; no direct sum of the whole family is assumed. The isomorphisms are data. **First quadrant** means the initial page vanishes unless p,q≥0; **third quadrant** means it vanishes unless p,q≤0. **Bounded** means that for each integer n only finitely many initial-page terms with p+q=n are nonzero. These support conditions persist because later terms are subquotients of earlier ones.

For the pages of a filtered complex there is a specified natural isomorphism
$$\alpha_r:H(E^r,d^r)_{p,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}E^{r+1}_{p,q}\qquad(r\ge0).$$
The homology at $(p,q)$ uses the incoming map from $(p+r,q-r+1)$ and outgoing map to $(p-r,q+r-1)$.

If the filtration on every $C_n$ is finite, the spectral sequence of the filtered chain complex stabilizes pointwise and naturally abuts to $H_n(C)$ with its image filtration. This homology filtration is finite, exhaustive and separated. No uniform filtration bound in n is required.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

For a finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ with $n$ ordered crossings, the procedure that enumerates all $2^n$ smoothing states, assigns one copy of $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ per resolution circle, places a generator in degrees $i=|v|-n_-$ and $j=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$, and sums the signed merge or split edge maps terminates after finitely many operations.
